name: Motorcycle
description: Any motor vehicle on no more than three wheels that isn't an autocycle, tractor, moped, EPAMD or electric bicycle, so an electric two-wheeler whose motor produces 2,000 watts or more is a motorcycle.

restrictions.rule: No more than three wheels in contact with the ground (Delaware Code Title 21 §101(41))

An electric two-wheeler of 2,000 watts or more is a motorcycle, as is one that is neither an e-bike nor a moped, such as one over 750 watts that can't pass 20 mph on its motor alone or 28 mph with pedaling (Delaware Code Title 21 §101(41), as amended by House Substitute 1 for HB 439)
Riders need a driver's license with a motorcycle endorsement
Riders under 18 must complete the state-approved Motorcycle Rider Education Course and have a parent's signature for the endorsement
A 60-day learner's permit allows no passengers, no riding between sunset and sunrise and no interstate highways, and requires a helmet and eye protection
Every rider and passenger must wear approved eye protection and carry an approved helmet
Riders and passengers under 19 must wear the helmet, as must a rider endorsed on or after July 30, 2023, and their passenger, for the first 2 years
Passengers only on a motorcycle built to carry one, with passenger footrests
Titled, registered and plated with the DMV, and must carry liability insurance
A motorcycle registered for the road is exempt from OHV registration

Sellers may not market or label an electric motorcycle as an e-bike or claim it is legal on a public pathway or bike lane, and must disclose in writing its legal class, motor power in watts and brake horsepower, top speed, and that registration, license and insurance rules apply (House Substitute 1 for HB 439)
